description: This program elective gives fundamental concepts of system identification, probability theory, random variables, non-parametric and parametric methods, non-recursive and recursive methods, and the basics of Kalman filter design.

syllabus.title: Probability and Random Processes
syllabus.body: Review of probability theory and random processes, problem formulation for identification and estimation.

syllabus.title: Models and Non-parametric Identification
syllabus.body: Models: review of continuous and discrete, state space and input-output, disturbance models. Identification: impulse response and transfer function approach (non-parametric methods).

syllabus.title: Parameter Estimation
syllabus.body: Introduction, maximum likelihood method, mean square method, linear regression and least-squares methods and their properties, prediction error approach.

syllabus.title: Recursive Methods and Kalman Filter
syllabus.body: Non-recursive and recursive methods, Kalman filter. Design exercises in MATLAB/LabVIEW and case studies.

outcomes: Understand statistical properties and modeling of systems with random variables.
Identify system models using identification methods in both transfer function and state space representation.
Understand the need for estimators and the estimation process for linear systems using different techniques.
Apply the theory learned to case studies and understand computational aspects in estimation and identification.
textbooks: Lennart Ljung, System Identification: Theory for the User, Prentice Hall Inc., NJ, 1991.
B. N. Chatterji and K. K. Parmer, System Identification Techniques, Oxford and IBH Publications, New Delhi, 1989.
A. Papoulis and S. U. Pillai, Probability, Random Variables and Stochastic Processes, 4th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2002.
referenceBooks: Arun K. Tangirala, Principles of System Identification: Theory and Practice, CRC Press, 2015.
